courseReview.name: Personal & Professional Development
courseReview.contribution: Mandatory first-year development.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Data Science
courseReview.contribution: Complementary empirical tool: cleaning, manipulating and visualising tabular, spatial and text data, with a cross-disciplinary research project. Biomedical datasets and patient contact are not guaranteed.

courseReview.name: Machine Learning
courseReview.contribution: Complementary quantitative tool: regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree methods, support-vector machines and clustering support predictive analysis. The course is general machine learning, not a biomedical bioinformatics sequence.

courseReview.name: Mathematical Methods
courseReview.contribution: provides mathematical foundations for the later probability and statistics course

courseReview.name: Probability & Statistics
courseReview.contribution: develops probability distributions, estimation and simulation for quantitative research

courseReview.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courseReview.contribution: Complementary conceptual foundation: knowledge, consciousness and philosophical argument prepare for the mind/emotion strand, rather than adding biomedical laboratory content.

courseReview.name: Ethics
courseReview.contribution: Complementary normative method: moral theories, responsibility and reasoned judgments support appraisal of biomedical choices. The actual practical cases are general ethics, not a dedicated biomedical research-integrity or clinical-ethics course.

courseReview.name: Philosophy of Mind
courseReview.contribution: Complementary conceptual inquiry: consciousness, personal identity, neurobiological explanations of mind and perceptual experience deepen the neuroscience route without substituting for experimental neuroscience.

courseReview.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courseReview.contribution: Complementary conceptual inquiry into emotions, rationality, well-being and moral judgment; this supports the neuroscience/mental-health question without claiming a clinical treatment course.

courseReview.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
courseReview.contribution: studies population patterns, disease risk and prevention through epidemiological evidence

courseReview.name: Functional Anatomy
courseReview.contribution: Direct human anatomy and function: body systems, surface anatomy, imaging, spatial reasoning and dissection-related academic encounters support biomedical mechanisms. These are academic learning experiences, not clinical-skills training.

courseReview.name: Pharmacology
courseReview.contribution: explains pharmacological action, therapeutic effects and toxicity of drugs

courseReview.name: Infection & Immunity
courseReview.contribution: studies pathogens, immune recognition and innate and adaptive defence

courseReview.name: Mechanisms of Disease
courseReview.contribution: compares normal physiology with disease mechanisms across cardiovascular, respiratory and other organ systems

courseReview.name: Neurobiology
courseReview.contribution: explores the neurobiology that underlies behaviour and physiological response

courseReview.name: Perception & Action
courseReview.contribution: studies sensory processing and neural control of action with cognitive-neuroscience methods

courseReview.name: Higher Order Functions
courseReview.contribution: develops advanced neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and cognitive-neuroscience experiment design

courseReview.name: Psycholinguistics
courseReview.contribution: studies neural and psychological mechanisms of language processing

courseReview.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
courseReview.contribution: introduces cells, molecules and organ systems as foundations for biomedical explanation

courseReview.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courseReview.contribution: introduces the biological and psychological study of brain and behaviour

courseReview.name: Molecular Cell Biology
courseReview.contribution: develops cellular mechanisms, including processes central to molecular disease biology

courseReview.name: Human Physiology
courseReview.contribution: examines regulation and functioning of adult human organ systems

courseReview.name: Biochemistry
courseReview.contribution: studies proteins, nucleic acids and metabolic reactions underlying cell function

courseReview.name: Life Science Laboratory
courseReview.contribution: provides hands-on biochemical and molecular laboratory techniques, including work with blood and microbes

courseReview.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
courseReview.contribution: examines human molecular pathology, genetics, inflammation and neoplasia

courseReview.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courseReview.contribution: Direct quantitative method: multivariate statistical modelling, linear/logistic regression, factor analysis, ANOVA/ANCOVA and non-parametric testing support biomedical evidence analysis. The actual enriched content is statistical modelling; the title does not establish a separate experimental-design syllabus.

courseReview.name: Abnormal Psychology
courseReview.contribution: examines mental disorders across the lifespan through biological, psychological and social explanations

courseReview.name: Medical & Health Psychology
courseReview.contribution: examines biological, psychological and social determinants of illness and health interventions

courseReview.name: Advanced Research Seminar
courseReview.contribution: Direct evidence-synthesis method: systematic review and meta-analysis using R estimate effects and compare evidence across studies. It does not supply a new primary biomedical experiment or the extended research internship.

courseReview.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
courseReview.contribution: studies psychological development across the lifespan, including interactions among developmental influences

academicReview: The closest route has sustained molecular, cellular, physiological, anatomical, pathological, pharmacological and immunological study with laboratory, population and quantitative methods. The second retains substantial biomedical mechanisms while prioritising neural/cognitive processes, language and mental health, with a bounded philosophy complement. Both answer material defining biomedical substance under the CP119 distinction; neither mere coherence nor gap disclaimers establish that conclusion. Six genuinely different courses per programme follow these priorities. Epidemiology/population health is evidenced but the available course subset does not sustain a further distinct population-methods programme; human movement lacks a sustained biomechanical/exercise-methods sequence; health technology assessment lacks the required specialist economic-evaluation sequence; toxicology has pharmacological and molecular support but no sustained distinct toxicology programme. Do not fill these candidates with weak adjacency. Stop at two.
